title: 8 Things to Check on Your JEE Main Admit Card Before Exam Day
description: The admit card is four pages of details where a single error can cause real trouble at the gate. Here are the 8 things to actually verify, and what to do if something's wrong.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Most students download their JEE Main admit card, glance at the exam date and centre, and move on. That's the minimum, not the full check. The admit card is a four-page document with a lot of specific fields, and an error on any of them is much easier to fix a week before the exam than at the gate on exam morning.

content.heading: The full checklist
content.body: Go through every one of these against your original application, not just from memory:

table.caption: The 8 checks
columns: What goes wrong if it's incorrect
rows: Name, father's name, date of birth
Exactly as on your photo ID
A mismatch with your ID can get you stopped at entry
Gender and category
Matches your application
The wrong cutoff and reservation rules get applied
State of eligibility
What you intended when applying
State-level counselling eligibility can be affected later
Roll number and application number
Both printed and legible
You need both for results and any correction request
Paper
Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech), Paper 2A (B.Arch) or Paper 2B (B.Planning)
You may be sitting a paper you didn't prepare for
Centre, date, shift and reporting time
Full address and city, not just the date
Wrong centre, or arriving after the gate closes
Photograph and signature
Clear and as uploaded, not cropped or corrupted
Identity checks at the gate can fail
Category certificate requirements
Any documents the guidelines list for you
Missing paperwork can hold up entry or verification

content.heading: The step students actually forget
content.body: The admit card isn't done once it's downloaded. It includes a self-declaration section where you need to paste a recent photograph and put your left-hand thumb impression before carrying it to the centre. Arriving with an admit card that's missing this step is treated the same as arriving with an incomplete one. Do this the same day you download it, not the morning of the exam when you're already rushed. One part you should not do at home: the signature. NTA's instructions are to sign the declaration only inside the exam hall, in front of the invigilator, so leave that box blank until you're told to sign.

content.heading: What to actually bring, not just download
content.body: The printed admit card alone isn't sufficient. A valid photo ID (the same one used during registration) is required alongside it, and entry is refused without both. Report before the gate closing time printed on the card, not the exam start time. Gates close before the exam begins, and "I was on time for the exam" doesn't help if you missed the gate closing.

content.heading: If you spot an error
content.body: Don't wait to see if it matters. Errors in personal details, category, or exam centre should be raised with NTA through the correct channel (the helpline or grievance portal listed on the official JEE Main website) as soon as you notice them. The earlier this happens relative to your exam date, the more realistic it is to get a fix processed in time.
